newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Waigel says France, Germany committed to EMU.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Waigel says France, Germany committed to EMU.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said France and Germany reaffirmed on Tuesday their commitment to keep up efforts to cut government spending in order to meet criteria for European currency union.

Waigel also said after a meeting of top financial officials here that both countries believed a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after currency union was essential for gaining public confidence in the new currency.
Despite the positive developments in the second quarter, Waigel said Germany must still "do all things necessary" to meet the Maastricht Treaty's criteria for currency union.

The treaty, which sets goals on interest and exchange rates, inflation and public budgets, calls for nations wanting to join currency union to have a budget deficit of no more than three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997.
Waigel said that Germany re-emphasised during the meeting that it would keep striving to get its budget deficit below three percent in 1997 with its cost-cutting policies.

Waigel made the comments at a news conference following a meeting, which included Waigel, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Bank of France President Jean-Claude Trichet.

The meeting, sandwiched between critical budget talks in Bonn and Paris this week, falls just three days ahead of an informal meeting of European Union finance officials in Dublin which will address key aspects of the single currency project.
Tietmeyer reiterated that Germany and France must still make major steps for a solid European currency union.

Tietmeyer also said criteria for currency union laid out in the Maastricht Treaty must be properly and precisely applied and that countries joining the new currency must be able to show they can maintain lasting stability.
"The goal is to ensure lasting growth and employment," he told a news conference after a Franco-German economic summit. But he stressed, "The criteria must be properly applied."
